Then, calculate the discriminant (Δ = b² - 4ac). If Δ > 0, there are two real and distinct roots. If Δ = 0, there is one real root. If Δ < 0, there are no real roots. Finally, use the quadratic formula x = [-b ± √(b² - 4ac)] / (2a) to find the roots.

To find the stationary points of a function y = f(x), first, find the first derivative of the function, f'(x). Then, set the first derivative equal to zero and solve for x. These x-values correspond to the stationary points of the function. To determine whether each stationary point is a local minimum, local maximum, or a saddle point, find the second derivative of the function, f''(x), and evaluate it at each stationary point. If f''(x) > 0, the stationary point is a local minimum. If f''(x) < 0, the stationary point is a local maximum. If f''(x) = 0, the stationary point is a saddle point.
